request:
SYNTHETIC PLANWORK RECOVERY FIXTURE. Plan the Aster Charts atomic import for its engine and shared iOS/macOS coordinator. The release owner has approved the acceptance wording below as the nine separate verification strings. Copy each complete numbered string into the JSON verification array, verbatim and in order. These are release handoff text and retain their specific UI and storage outcomes. For the changes array write five compact technical implementation entries covering the canonical UID and schema, preview state, atomic compare-and-swap and receipt, shared UI failure mapping, and rollout. Cite exactly box/charts:README.md and box/native-apple:README.md in the citations array. Keep goal and gaps brief and set issueTemplate and issueBody to null. Return full valid JSON.

HANDOFF-01 Preview. Given revision R4 and Dashboard Alpha with panels CPU and Memory, open preview on both client shells. When the shared coordinator resolves the file, show canonical UID alpha, current revision R4, and unresolved datasource local-metrics. Then inspect the stored dashboard table and the activity log and verify both remain unchanged while the user considers the preview.

HANDOFF-02 Normalization. Given an empty catalog and drafts with UIDs Alpha and alpha surrounded by whitespace, run validation in each shell before confirming either. When normalized identifiers are compared, use one canonical key alpha. Then assert deterministic identity matching and inspect distinct readable display titles, while preserving the original source files and avoiding any write during validation.

HANDOFF-03 Malformed. Given valid JSON with an unsupported schema version and an invalid panel expression, open preview and inspect the normalized error list. When the validation boundary rejects the definition, assert separate field-level messages for schemaVersion and the named panel. Then inspect persistent state, revision and activity before and after to verify that each remains unchanged.

HANDOFF-04 Fresh Confirm. Given a valid dashboard preview at revision R4, confirm request SYN-A on the client while no other writer has persisted a revision. When storage matches R4, atomically install the complete normalized dashboard and activity with revision R5. Then show the returned canonical UID and R5 in the catalog, with one durable successful request receipt.

HANDOFF-05 Stale Confirm. Given the same preview at R4, commit an independent change through the second client to produce R5 before confirming request SYN-B. When the first client confirms, assert that storage rejects the stale revision. Then keep R5 and its activity unchanged, show the newer revision in the stale-preview message, and require a fresh preview and confirmation.

HANDOFF-06 Different Writers. Given two valid previews targeting the same UID at R4, confirm two different request IDs concurrently through the coordinator. When storage serializes the writes, exactly one compare-and-swap reaches R5 and the other returns a conflict. Then confirm that neither the dashboard nor the activity log contains partial changes or a second successful commit.

HANDOFF-07 Duplicate Receipt. Given a committed request SYN-C whose first response was interrupted, submit the identical request again before refreshing the catalog. When the coordinator finds the durable receipt, return the original revision, canonical UID and outcome. Then check that a retry with a changed request fingerprint is rejected and that only one activity record exists.

HANDOFF-08 Storage Rollback. Given a valid R4 preview and a fixture that fails after writing the proposed dashboard within the transaction, confirm and observe the typed storage failure. When the database rolls back the transaction, preserve R4, the existing dashboard and its activity. Then retry after recovery and verify precisely one successful commit and no duplicate receipt.

HANDOFF-09 Cancel. Given a confirmed read-only preview in each client shell, cancel before submission and navigate back to the catalog. When the coordinator discards the preview, keep the current revision and activity unchanged. Then reopen the file to show a freshly loaded preview so an old candidate cannot survive a cancelled navigation and accidentally submit later.
